data: この 荷物[にもつ]を 預[あず]かって まら えますか？
Can you hold this luggage for me?
Travel
預かる (あずかる, azukaru) means "to keep or hold onto something for someone," and まらえますか (moraemasu ka) is a polite request form asking if the action is possible.
この 国[くに]に ある 1029[せんにじゅうきゅう]城[じょう]は、 全[すべ]て トーフグの ものだ。
All 1,029 castles in this country are Tofugu's.
Counter,Somewhat Common
城 · じょう · Castles, palaces.

What is the price of breakfast?

朝食 (ちょうしょく, choushoku) means "breakfast," and 値段 (ねだん, nedan) means "price."
存在[そんざい] する 意味[いみ]が ない。

Do you have a room for tonight?

今晩 (こんばん, konban) means "tonight," and 部屋 (へや, heya) means "room."
予約[よやく]を 確認[かくにん] したいんですが
I would like to confirm the reservation.
Travel
確認 (かくにん, kakunin) means "confirmation."
支配[しはい]人[にん]を 呼[よ]んでください。
Please call the manager
Travel
支配人 (しはいにん, shihainin) means "manager," and 呼んでください (よんでください, yonde kudasai) is a polite request form of "to call."
部屋[へや]に カギを 置[お]き忘[わす]れました
I forgot to leave the key in the room
Travel
部屋 (へや, heya) means "room," カギ (かぎ, kagi) means "key," and 置き忘れる (おきわすれる, okiwasureru) means "to forget to leave."
階段[かいだん]を ２[に]段[だん] 飛[と]ばしで 上[のぼ]った。
I ran up the stairs, two at a time.
Counter,Common

段 · だん · Stairs, steps, shelves, the number of drawers, layers, floors of a bunk bed, stages of a rocket, ranks in martial arts, paragraphs, and even columns. What do these things have in common? Despite being totally different, they also all have pretty distinct layers/levels to them, and they're organized vertically (for the most part).
あそこの 券売[けんばい] 機[き]で 買[か]えますよ。
You can buy it at that ticket machine.
鼠,Travel
預[あず]けた 荷物[にもつ]を 出[だ]したいんですが
I would like to retrieve the luggage I left
Travel
預ける (あずける, azukeru) means "to entrust" or "to leave," and 出す (だす, dasu) means "to take out" or "retrieve."
難[むずか]しい 問題[もんだい]が 3[さん]題[だい]も 出題[しゅつだい] された。
There were three difficult questions.
Counter,Somewhat Common
題 · だい · Titles, problems, and questions on a test. It can be combined with the ordinal number prefix 代 and the ordinal number suffix 目 to refer to specific problems or questions.
マフラーを 首[くび]に 2[に]巻[かん] きして 外[そと]に 出[で]た。
I wrapped the scarf around my neck twice and went outside.
Counter,Somewhat Common
巻/巻き · まき · How many times something has been rolled, wrapped or coiled around another thing.
この 段落[だんらく]、 2[に] 段落[だんらく]に 分[わ]けた 方[ほう]が いいんじゃない?
Wouldn't it be better to separate this paragraph in two?
Counter,Somewhat Common
段落 · だんらく · Paragraphs and stages of tasks.
トイ・ ストーリー・ シリーズを、 2[に] 夜[よる] 連続[れんぞく]で お届[とど]けします。
We're going to air the Toy Story series two nights in a row.
Counter,Somewhat Common
夜 · や/よ · Nights. Normally, it's read with kango using the や reading for 夜, but one and two nights can also be counted with the wago readings. When that happens, 夜 becomes よ.
この プロジェクトを 達成[たっせい] するには、 2[に] 段階[だんかい]の フェーズが あります。
There are two phases to accomplishing this project.
Counter,Somewhat Common
段階 · だんかい · Steps—not stairsteps, but stages or phases.
この E ブックには、 トーフグの 短編[たんぺん]が 1029[せんにじゅうきゅう]編[へん] 収録[しゅうろく] されています。
This ebook contains 1,029 of Tofugu's short stories.
Counter,Somewhat Common
編/篇 · へん · Poems, pieces of writing, and other smaller units within the world of writing.

予約[よやく]の 再[さい]確認[かくにん] したいんですが
I would like to reconfirm my reservation.
Travel
再確認 (さいかくにん, saikakunin) means "reconfirmation," and the sentence ends with the same "but" (が) to indicate the speaker’s further request.
二人[ふたり]で 過[す]ごした 時[とき]を 忘[わす]れない。
I won't forget the time that we spent together.
Emotion
１００[ひゃく]枚[まい]の 折[お]り紙[がみ]が 必要[ひつよう]です。
I need 100 pieces of origami paper.
Counter,Must Know
枚 · まい · Flat things.
あなたは 人[ひと]の 感情[かんじょう]を 尊重[そんちょう] する。
You respect other people's feelings.
Emotion
コウイチは 毎日[まいにち] ７[なな]冊[さつ] 本[ほん]を 読[よ]みます。
Koichi reads seven books every day.
Counter,Must Know
冊 · さつ · Books.
だれか 英語[えいご]を 話[はな]せる 人[ひと]を 探[さが]してみます
I will try to find someone who can speak English.
Travel

だれか (dareka) means "someone," 英語 (えいご, eigo) means "English," 話せる (はなせる, hanaseru) is the potential form of "speak," meaning "can speak." 人 (ひと, hito) means "person." 探してみます (さがしてみます, sagashite mimasu) means "I will try to find," with 探す (さがす, sagasu) meaning "to search."
ダリンは 1[いち]輪[りん]車[しゃ]に 乗[の]って 通勤[つうきん] している。
Darin comes to work by unicycle.
Counter,Somewhat Common
輪 · りん · Circles, rings, hoops, wheels, flowers (because the petals make a circle), and crowns of flowers.
この 建物[たてもの]には、 礼拝[れいはい]堂[どう]が 3[さん]堂[どう] あります。
In this building, there are three chapels.
Counter,Somewhat Common
堂 · どう · Chapels, temples, shrines, halls, lecture halls, auditoriums, assembly halls, churches, cathedrals, etc.
その 電車[でんしゃ]の 座席[ざせき]を 予約[よやく] したいんですが
I would like to reserve a seat on that train.
Travel
座席 (ざせき, zaseki) means "seat," and 予約 (よやく, yoyaku) means "reservation."
2[に]男[なん] 2[に]女[じょ]の 子供[こども]を 持[も]つ ことが 夢[ゆめ]なんです。
My dream is to have two sons and two daughters.
Counter,Somewhat Common

男 · なん · Sons. They're read using the kango readings, but two is an exception—instead of に, it's read as じ. It can also be used as an ordinal number suffix, but one and two become 長男 (ちょうなん) and 次男 (じなん).
手[て] 荷物[にもつ] 一[いち]時[じ] 預[あず]かり所[しょ]
Temporary luggage storage, daily luggage storage
Travel
手荷物 (てにもつ, tenimotsu) means "luggage," 一時 (いちじ, ichiji) means "temporary," and 預かり所 (あずかりじょ, azukari-jo) means "storage."
この 歯[は] 医者[いしゃ]には、 いつも 週刊[しゅうかん]誌[し]が ４[よん]誌[し] 置[お]いてある。
This dentist always carries four different weekly magazines.
Counter,Somewhat Common
誌 · し · Magazines, tabloids.
44[よんじゅうよん]隊[たい]の 探検[たんけん]隊[たい]が この ジャングルで 行方[ゆくえ] 不明[ふめい]になった。
Forty-four expedition teams went missing in this jungle.
Counter,Somewhat Common
隊 · たい · Corps, units, parties, troops, and so on.
カナエの 机[つくえ]の 上[うえ]には、 88[はちじゅうはち]体[たい]の コウイチ 人形[にんぎょう]が 8[はち] 列[れつ]に 並[なら]べられていた。
On Kanae's desk, there were eighty-eight Koichi dolls arranged in eight lines.
Counter,Somewhat Common
列 · れつ · Lines or queues of people, rows of things in lines.
今日[きょう]は 編[あ]み物[もの]で 1[いち]目[もく] 落[お]としてしまった 時[とき]の 対処[たいしょ] 方法[ほうほう]を みなさんに お教[おし]えます。
Today, I'm gonna teach you how to pick up a dropped stitch in knitting.
Counter,Somewhat Common

目 · め · Words that use 目 in their name, not physical eyeballs. 目 can be used as an ordinal number suffix after the general counter ~つ. For example, 一つ目 is "the first one," 二つ目 is "the second one," and so on.

ジュースを ９[きゅう]杯[はい]も おかわり した。

Counter,Common

杯 · はい · Liquids in cups or bowls. That means you can count things like bowls of soup, mugs of coffee, glasses of juice, measuring spoons of vanilla, measuring cups of chicken broth, and so on. In addition, you can use 杯 to count squid, cuttlefish, crabs, and sometimes octopuses. 杯 can also count ships, battleships, racing yachts, and other boats, but this usage isn't so common.

乾杯[かんぱい]！
Cheers!
Travel
乾杯 (かんぱい, kanpai) is a toast used when drinking with others, much like "Cheers!" in English. It literally means "dry glass," referring to drinking all of the contents in your glass.

こちらで お支払[しはら]い できます

This informs the customer that payment can be made at this location. こちら (kochira) means "here," で (de) marks the location, お支払い (oshiharai) is the polite form of "pay," and できます (dekimasu) indicates ability (can do).

ビニール 袋[ふくろ]ですか、 紙袋[かみぶくろ]ですか？
Would you like a plastic or paper bag?
Travel
This question offers the customer a choice of bag types. ビニール袋 (bini-ru fukuro) means "plastic bag," 紙袋 (kami fukuro) means "paper bag," and ですか (desu ka) is the question form.
もっと 甘[あま]さを 強[つよ]めにしてください
Please make it sweeter.
Travel

もっと (motto) means "more," 甘さ (amasa) means "sweetness," and 強めに (tsuyome ni) means "stronger" or "more intense." してください (shite kudasai) is a polite way to say "please do," requesting someone to take action. This phrase is a polite way to ask for something to be made sweeter.
その まま お召[め]し上[あ]がりください。
Please eat it as is.
鼠,Travel
ツナ 缶[かん] ５[ご]缶[かん]と コーラ １２[じゅうに]缶[かん]を 買[か]った。
I bought five cans of tuna and twelve cans of cola.
Counter,Common

缶 · かん · This word means can (as in an aluminum can). Its reading is (coincidentally) "kan", and it can be used to count cans. The first two cans can be counted with either wago or kango numbers. "One can" is １缶, read as either いっかん or ひとかん. "Two cans" is ２缶, read as either にかん or ふたかん. From three cans and up you use the kango counting method. When a can is empty—or when it's a garbage can—you'll generally want to use the counter 個 instead of 缶.
ほかの ホテルを 紹介[しょうかい] してくれませんか？
Can you recommend another hotel?
Travel
ほかの (hoka no) means "other," and 紹介してくれませんか (しょうかいしてくれませんか, shoukai shite kuremasen ka) is a polite request for a recommendation.
バスを 乗[の]り換[か]えなければいけませんか？
Do I have to transfer buses?
Travel
バス (basu) means "bus." 乗り換え (のりかえ, norikae) means "transfer." なければいけません (nakereba ikemasen) is the negative obligation form, meaning "must." か (ka) turns it into a question.

注文[ちゅうもん] した ものと 違[ちが]います
This is not what I ordered.

注文した (chūmon shita) means "ordered," with 注文 (chūmon) meaning "order" and した (shita) being the past tense of "to do." もの (mono) means "thing" or "item." と (to) is a particle meaning "with" or "and," used here to connect "what I ordered" with the rest of the sentence. 違います (chigaimasu) means "is different" or "is incorrect," and it is the polite form.
